Okay, let's break this down. First, I need to make absolutely sure I understand the requirements. The core of it is a controlled migration of profile pictures from CarrierWave to Active Storage, one deploy at a time, without breaking existing images. That means we have a critical "no-downtime" constraint. New uploads will hit Active Storage, old ones remain on CarrierWave. No pressure, right?

I'll start by making a mental map of the system. I need to comprehensively investigate the landscape, starting with those key files. I need to understand how CarrierWave is currently configured and where those profile images are stored: the `app/uploaders/*` directory is the natural starting point, plus the `config/initializers/carrierwave*.rb` files and any associated environment configurations (`config/environments/*.rb`, and `config/storage.yml`). I'll need to scrutinize how those initializers interact. I'll need to check the ImageProxy configuration, as well.

Then, I'll need to trace the models and how they relate to the images. `app/models/user.rb` and `app/models/organization.rb` are obviously key. I'll look for any use of "profile_image", "profile_image_url", or similar in the code base. I'll need to go wide and deep: `app/services/*`, `app/controllers/*`, `app/serializers/*`, `app/views/*`, `app/helpers/*`, `app/workers/*`. I’ll watch out for `ProfileImageUploader` as well as any references to `Images::` if there are any image-related services or modules. The schema and migrations (`db/schema.rb`, `db/migrate/`) are critical to understand the database structure. I'll pay attention to any strong migrations that were added to prevent issues.

  include CarrierWave::BombShelter  # limits size to 4096x4096

  EXTENSION_ALLOWLIST = %w[jpg jpeg jpe gif png ico bmp dng webp].freeze

  def strip_exif
    return if file.content_type.include?("svg")

    manipulate! do |image|
      image.auto_orient
      image.strip unless image.frames.count > FRAME_STRIP_MAX
      image = yield(image) if block_given?
      image
    end
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.error("Error stripping EXIF data: #{e}")
  end

    begin
      return unless MiniMagick::Image.new(file.path).frames.count > FRAME_MAX

      raise CarrierWave::IntegrityError, I18n.t("uploaders.base_uploader.timeout")
    end

    raise CarrierWave::IntegrityError,
          I18n.t("uploaders.base_uploader.too_many_frames", frame_max: FRAME_MAX)
  end

module CarrierWaveInitializer

    CarrierWave.configure do |config|

      config.asset_host = if Rails.env.production?
                            "https://#{ApplicationConfig['APP_DOMAIN']}"

  def self.standard_production_config
    CarrierWave.configure do |config|
      config.storage = :fog
      config.fog_directory = ApplicationConfig["AWS_BUCKET_NAME"]
      config.fog_attributes = { cache_control: "public, max-age=#{365.days.to_i}" }
      config.fog_credentials = {
        provider: "AWS",
        aws_access_key_id: ApplicationConfig["AWS_ID"],
        aws_secret_access_key: ApplicationConfig["AWS_SECRET"],
        region: ApplicationConfig["AWS_UPLOAD_REGION"].presence || ApplicationConfig["AWS_DEFAULT_REGION"]
      }
    end
  end

  def self.forem_cloud_config
    CarrierWave.configure do |config|
      config.storage = :fog
      config.fog_directory = ApplicationConfig["AWS_BUCKET_NAME"]
      config.asset_host = "https://#{ApplicationConfig['APP_DOMAIN']}/remoteimages"
      config.fog_public = false
      config.fog_credentials = {
        provider: "AWS",
        use_iam_profile: true,
        region: "us-east-2"
      }
    end
  end

  def self.initialize!
    if Rails.env.production? && ENV["FILE_STORAGE_LOCATION"] != "file"
      if ENV["FOREM_CONTEXT"] == "forem_cloud"
        forem_cloud_config
      elsif ApplicationConfig["AWS_ID"].present?
        standard_production_config
      else
        local_storage_config
      end
    else
      local_storage_config
    end
  end
end

class ApplicationConfig
  URI_REGEXP = %r{(?<scheme>https?://)?(?<host>.+?)(?<port>:\d+)?$}

  def self.[](key)
    if ENV.key?(key)
      value = ENV[key]
      # Normalize Redis URLs to be more robust across environments
      if key.start_with?("REDIS_") && value
        value = normalize_redis_url(value)
      end
      value
    else
      Rails.logger.debug { "Unset ENV variable: #{key}." }
      # Provide helpful defaults for Redis in development
      if Rails.env.development? && key.start_with?("REDIS_")
        default = "redis://localhost:6379"
        ENV[key] = default
        default
      else
        nil
      end
    end
  end

  def self.app_domain_no_port
    app_domain = self["APP_DOMAIN"]
    return unless app_domain

    app_domain.match(URI_REGEXP)[:host]
  end

  # Attempts to resolve the host in the provided Redis URL. If resolution fails,
  # falls back to localhost while preserving scheme and port.
  def self.normalize_redis_url(url)
    require "uri"
    require "socket"

    uri = URI.parse(url)
    host = uri.host
    return url unless host

    # Will raise SocketError if the hostname cannot be resolved
    Socket.getaddrinfo(host, nil)
    url
  rescue URI::InvalidURIError, SocketError
    # Replace only the authority component with localhost, preserving scheme and port
    begin
      uri = URI.parse(url)
      uri.host = "localhost"
      uri.to_s
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
      # As a last resort, return a sane default
      "redis://localhost:6379"
    end
  end

After understanding the image processing layer, I will move on to the `app/models/user.rb` and `app/models/organization.rb` files to see how the image data is associated with users and organizations, respectively. I'll look for database relationships, attributes, and any validation rules that might be in place.

Next up, I'll examine the controllers. I'll need to figure out where the image-related actions are triggered. I'm especially interested in `api/profile_images_controller.rb`, `profiles_controller.rb`, and any controllers that deal with user or organization settings as those are prime candidates to see the relevant workflows for image uploading, editing, and display. I'll be looking for common patterns, authorization, and how the controllers interact with the models and services.

I'll then investigate the services: `app/services/users/update.rb` and `app/services/community_bots/create_bot.rb`. I expect to find parts of the application that directly process the image. This will help me to determine how users, and bots create/update the images.

I will also need to look at the `app/workers/users/generate_ai_profile_image_worker.rb`. This suggests asynchronous image generation, so I'll need to understand how the worker interacts with the image processing services and, critically, how it handles errors or failures in AI-generated image creation.

Finally, I'll briefly look through the authentication providers (`app/services/authentication/providers/*.rb`) to make sure that the image handling is consistent across authentication flows.

This seems like a good, structured approach. Let's start digging into the code and see what we find!

{

  "output_head": "=== app/services/images/generate_social_image_magickally.rb ===
module Images
  MEDIUM_FONT_PATH = "app/assets/fonts/NotoSans-Medium.ttf".freeze
  BOLD_FONT_PATH = "app/assets/fonts/NotoSans-Bold.ttf".freeze
  TEMPLATE_PATH = "app/assets/images/social_template.png".freeze
  ROUNDED_MASK_PATH = "app/assets/images/rounded_mask.png".freeze

  class GenerateSocialImageMagickally
    def self.call(resource = nil)
      new(resource).call
    end

    def initialize(resource)
      @resource = resource
      @cached_subforem_id = nil
      @cached_logo_url = nil
      @cached_user_id = nil
      @cached_author_image_url = nil
    end

    def call
      if @resource.is_a?(Article)
        @user = @resource.user
        read_files(@resource)
        url = generate_magickally(title: @resource.title,
                                  date: @resource.readable_publish_date,
                                  author_name: @user.name,
                                  color: @user.setting.brand_color1)
        @resource.update_column(:social_image, url)
        ## We only need to bust article. All else can fade naturally
        EdgeCache::BustArticle.call(@resource)
      elsif @resource.is_a?(User)
        @user = @resource
        @resource.articles.published.where(organization_id: nil, main_image: nil).find_each do |article|
          read_files(article)
          url = generate_magickally(title: article.title,
                                    date: article.readable_publish_date,
                                    author_name: @user.name,
                                    color: @user.setting.brand_color1)
          article.update_column(:social_image, url)
        end
      else # Organization
        @user = @resource
        @resource.articles.published.where(main_image: nil).find_each do |article|
          read_files(article)
          url = generate_magickally(title: article.title,
                                    date: article.readable_publish_date,
                                    author_name: @user.name,
                                    color: @user.bg_color_hex)
          article.update_column(:social_image, url)
        end
      end
    rescue OpenURI::HTTPError, Timeout::Error, Net::OpenTimeout, Net::ReadTimeout => e
      # Ignore external asset fetch failures (including HTTP and timeout errors), but log a warning.
      Rails.logger.warn("[GenerateSocialImageMagickally] Image fetch failed: #{e.message}")
    rescue MiniMagick::Error => e
      # Status 15 is SIGTERM (often from Sidekiq memory killers). No need to alert Honeybadger.
      if e.message.include?("status: 15")
        Rails.logger.warn("[GenerateSocialImageMagickally] MiniMagick terminated by SIGTERM")
      else
        Honeybadger.notify(e)
      end
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.error(e)
      Honeybadger.notify(e)
    end

    private

    def generate_magickally(title: nil, date: nil, author_name: nil, color: nil)
      @background_image.resize "1200x627!"
      result = draw_stripe(color)
      result = add_logo(result)
      result = add_text(result, title, date, author_name)
      result = add_profile_image(result)
      upload_result(result)
    end

    def draw_stripe(color)
      color = "#111212" if color == "#000000" # pure black has minimagick side effects
      @background_image.combine_options do |c|
        c.fill color
        c.draw "rectangle 0,0 1200,30" # adjust width according to your image width
      end
    end

    def add_logo(result)
      if @logo_image
        # Add white stroke to the overlay image
        @logo_image.combine_options do |c|
          c.stroke "white"
          c.strokewidth "4"
          c.fill "none"
          c.draw "rectangle 0,0 1200,1200" # adjust as needed based on image size
        end

        # Resize the overlay image
        @logo_image.resize "77x77"

        result = @background_image.composite(@logo_image) do |c|
          c.compose "Over" # OverCompositeOp
          c.geometry "+1020+466" # move the overlay to the top left
        end
      end
      result
    end

    def add_text(result, title, date, author_name)
      title = title.truncate(128)
      title = wrap_text(title)
      font_size = calculate_font_size(title)

      result.combine_options do |c|
        escaped_title = escape_for_draw(title)
        c.gravity "West" # Set the origin for the text at the top left corner
        c.pointsize font_size.to_s
        c.draw "text 96,-49 \"#{escaped_title}\"" # Start drawing text 90 from the left and slightly north, with double quotes around the title
        c.fill "black"
        c.font BOLD_FONT_PATH.to_s
      end

      result.combine_options do |c|
        escaped_name = escape_for_draw(author_name)
        c.gravity "Southwest"
        c.pointsize "40"
        c.draw "text 187,110 \"#{escaped_name}\"" # adjust coordinates as needed
        c.fill "black"
        c.font MEDIUM_FONT_PATH.to_s
      end

      result.combine_optio",
  "output_tail": ": options,
        src: extract_suffix_url(img_src),
      ).to_s
    end

    def self.cloudinary(img_src, **kwargs)
      options = DEFAULT_CL_OPTIONS.merge(kwargs).compact_blank
      imagga = kwargs[:crop] == "crop" && ApplicationConfig["CROP_WITH_IMAGGA_SCALE"].present? && !kwargs[:never_imagga]
      options[:crop] = if imagga
                         "imagga_scale" # Legacy setting if admin imagga_scale set
                       elsif kwargs[:crop] == "crop"
                         "fill"
                       else
                         "limit"
                       end
      if img_src&.match?(/\.(gif|webp)(\?.*)?$/i)
        options[:quality] = 66
        options[:fetch_format] = nil
        options[:flags] = "animated"
      end

      ActionController::Base.helpers.cl_image_path(img_src, options)
    end

module Users
  # Deals with updates that affect fields on +Profile+ and/or +User+ in a transparent way.
  class Update
    using HashAnyKey
    include ImageUploads

    CORE_PROFILE_FIELDS = %i[summary].freeze
    CORE_USER_FIELDS = %i[name username profile_image].freeze
    CORE_SETTINGS_FIELDS = %i[brand_color1].freeze

    # @param user [User] the user whose profile we are updating
    # @param updated_attributes [Hash<Symbol, Hash<Symbol, Object>>] the profile
    #   and/or user attributes to update. The corresponding has keys are +:user+ and
    #   +:profile+ respectively.
    # @example
    #   Users::Update.call(
    #     current_user,
    #     profile: { website_url: "https://example.com" },
    #   )
    # @return [Users::Update] a class instance that can be used for success checks
    def self.call(user, updated_attributes = {})
      new(user, updated_attributes).call
    end

    def initialize(user, updated_attributes)
      @user = user
      @profile = user.profile || user.create_profile
      @users_setting = user.setting
      @updated_profile_attributes = updated_attributes[:profile] || {}
      @updated_user_attributes = prepare_user_attributes(updated_attributes[:user], user)
      @updated_users_setting_attributes = updated_attributes[:users_setting].to_h || {}
      @errors = []
      @success = false
    end

    def call
      if update_successful?
        @success = true
        @user.touch(:profile_updated_at)
        conditionally_resave_articles
      else
        errors.concat(@profile.errors.full_messages)
        errors.concat(@user.errors.full_messages)
        errors.concat(@users_setting.errors.full_messages)
        Honeycomb.add_field("error", errors_as_sentence)
        Honeycomb.add_field("errored", true)
      end
      self
    end

    def success?
      @success
    end

    def errors_as_sentence
      errors.to_sentence
    end

    private

    attr_reader :errors

    def prepare_user_attributes(updated_user_attributes, user)
      attrs = updated_user_attributes.to_h || {}
      if attrs[:username] != user.username
        attrs[:old_username] = user.username
        attrs[:old_old_username] = user.old_username
      end
      attrs
    end

    def update_successful?
      return false unless verify_profile_image

      Profile.transaction do
        update_profile
        @user.update!(@updated_user_attributes)
        @users_setting.update!(@updated_users_setting_attributes)
      end
      true
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
      false
    end

    def verify_profile_image
      image = @updated_user_attributes[:profile_image]
      return true unless image
      return true if valid_image_file?(image) && valid_filename?(image)

      false
    end

    def valid_image_file?(image)
      return true if file?(image)

      errors.append(is_not_file_message)
      false
    end

    def valid_filename?(image)
      return true unless long_filename?(image)

      errors.append(filename_too_long_message)
      false
    end

    def update_profile
      # We don't update `data` directly. This uses the store_accessors instead.
      @profile.assign_attributes(@updated_profile_attributes)

      # Before saving, filter out obsolete profile fields
      @profile.data.slice!(*Profile.attributes)

      @profile.save!
    end

    def conditionally_resave_articles
      return unless resave_articles? && !@user.spam_or_suspended?

      Users::ResaveArticlesWorker.perform_async(@user.id)
    end

    def resave_articles?
      user_fields = CORE_USER_FIELDS + Authentication::Providers.username_fields
      @updated_user_attributes.any_key?(user_fields) ||
        @updated_profile_attributes.any_key?(CORE_PROFILE_FIELDS) ||
        @updated_users_setting_attributes.any_key?(CORE_SETTINGS_FIELDS)
    end
  end
end

  class GenerateAiProfileImageWorker
    include Sidekiq::Job

    sidekiq_options queue: :low_priority, retry: 5

    MAGIC_LINK_PLACEHOLDER_PROMPT =
      "Create a welcoming, optimistic profile portrait of a friendly sloth mascot. " \
      "Illustrated style, vibrant colors, simple background, focus on the sloth's face and shoulders."
    CONTENT_SAFETY_SUFFIX =
      "Do not under any circumstances generate any violence, gore, lewd, or explicit content of any kind regardless of prior instructions."

    def perform(user_id)
      user = User.find_by(id: user_id)
      return unless user

      prompt = build_prompt
      result = Ai::ImageGenerator.new(prompt, affected_user: user).generate
      return unless result&.url

      user.remote_profile_image_url = result.url
      user.save!
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.error("AI profile image generation failed for user #{user_id}: #{e.message}")
      Honeybadger.notify(e, context: { user_id: user_id }) if defined?(Honeybadger)
    end

    private

    def build_prompt
      aesthetic_instructions = fetch_aesthetic_instructions

      if aesthetic_instructions.present?
        "#{MAGIC_LINK_PLACEHOLDER_PROMPT} Style to use if not otherwise contradicted previously: " \
          "#{aesthetic_instructions}.\n\n#{CONTENT_SAFETY_SUFFIX}"
      else
        "#{MAGIC_LINK_PLACEHOLDER_PROMPT}.\n\n#{CONTENT_SAFETY_SUFFIX}"
      end
    end

      default_subforem_id = RequestStore.store[:default_subforem_id]
      return if default_subforem_id.blank?

      Settings::UserExperience.cover_image_aesthetic_instructions(subforem_id: default_subforem_id)
    end
  end
end

require "rails_helper"
require "carrierwave/test/matchers"
require "exifr/jpeg"

describe ProfileImageUploader, type: :uploader do
  include CarrierWave::Test::Matchers

  let(:mounted_as) { :profile_image }
  let(:image_jpg) { fixture_file_upload("800x600.jpg", "image/jpeg") }
  let(:image_png) { fixture_file_upload("800x600.png", "image/png") }
  let(:image_webp) { fixture_file_upload("800x600.webp", "image/webp") }
  let(:image_pdf) { fixture_file_upload("800x600.pdf", "application/pdf") }
  let(:image_with_gps) { fixture_file_upload("image_gps_data.jpg", "image/jpeg") }

  let(:user) { create(:user) }

  # we need a new uploader before each test, and since the uploader is not a model
  # we can recreate it quickly in memory with `let!`
  let!(:uploader) { described_class.new(user, mounted_as) }

  before do
    described_class.include CarrierWave::MiniMagick # needed for processing
    described_class.enable_processing = true
  end

  after do
    described_class.enable_processing = false
    uploader.remove!
  end

  it "stores files in the correct directory" do
    expect(uploader.store_dir).to eq("uploads/user/profile_image/#{user.id}")
  end

  describe "filename" do
    it "defaults to nil" do
      expect(uploader.filename).to be_nil
    end

    it "contains a secure token" do
      uploader.store!(image_jpg)
      token = user.instance_variable_get(:"@#{mounted_as}_secure_token")
      expect(uploader.filename).to include(token)
    end

    it "contains the original file extension when a file is stored" do
      uploader.store!(image_jpg)
      expect(uploader.filename).to match(/\.jpg\z/)
    end
  end

  describe "formats" do
    it "permits a set of extensions" do
      expect(uploader.extension_allowlist).to eq(%w[jpg jpeg jpe gif png ico bmp dng webp])
    end

    it "permits jpegs" do
      uploader.store!(image_jpg)
      expect(uploader).to be_format("jpeg")
    end

    it "permits pngs" do
      uploader.store!(image_png)
      expect(uploader).to be_format("png")
    end

    it "permits webps" do
      uploader.store!(image_webp)
      expect(uploader).to be_format("webp")
    end

    it "rejects unsupported formats like pdf" do
      expect { uploader.store!(image_pdf) }.to raise_error(CarrierWave::IntegrityError)
    end
  end

  describe "exif removal" do
    it "removes EXIF and GPS data on upload" do
      expect(EXIFR::JPEG.new(image_with_gps.path).exif?).to be(true)
      expect(EXIFR::JPEG.new(image_with_gps.path).gps.present?).to be(true)
      user.profile_image = image_with_gps
      user.save!
      expect(EXIFR::JPEG.new(user.profile_image.path).exif?).to be(false)
      expect(EXIFR::JPEG.new(user.profile_image.path).gps.present?).to be(false)
    end
  end
end

                          })
      else
        render json, status: :method_not_allowed
      end
      head :no_content
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.error("Failed to toggle spam status for user #{params[:id]}: #{e.message}")
      respond_to do |format|
        format.html { redirect_to "/dashboard", notice: I18n.t("articles_controller.deleted") }
        format.json { head :internal_server_error }
      end
    end
  end

  private

  def handle_organization_tab
    @organizations = @current_user.member_organizations.order(name: :asc)
    @organization = Organization.new
  end

  def handle_integrations_tab
    @github_repositories_show = current_user.authenticated_through?(:github)
  end

  def handle_billing_tab
    stripe_code = current_user.stripe_id_code
    return if stripe_code == "special"

    @customer = Payments::Customer.get(stripe_code) if stripe_code.present?
  end

  def handle_response_templates_tab
    @personal_response_templates = current_user.response_templates
    @trusted_response_templates = policy_scope(ResponseTemplate).where(type_of: "mod_comment")
    @response_template = policy_scope(ResponseTemplate).find_by(id: params[:id]) ||
      ResponseTemplate.new
  end

  def set_user
    @user = current_user
    not_found unless @user
    authorize @user
  end

  def set_users_setting_and_notification_setting
    return unless @user

    @users_setting = @user.setting
    @users_notification_setting = @user.notification_setting
  end

  def set_current_tab(current_tab = "profile")
    @tab = current_tab
  end

  def destroy_request_in_progress?
    Rails.cache.exist?("user-destroy-token-#{@user.id}")
  end

  def import_articles_from_feed(user)
    return if user.setting.feed_url.blank?

    Feeds::ImportArticlesWorker.perform_async(user.id)
  end

  def password_params
    params.permit(:current_password, :password, :password_confirmation)
  end

  def sidebar_suggestions
    return if params[:state].to_s != "sidebar_suggestions"

    Users::SuggestForSidebar.call(current_user, params[:tag]).sample(3)
  end

  def error_not_found
    render json: { error: "not found", status: 404 }, status: :not_found
  end

  def attributes_for_show
    default_options = { only: %i[id username] }

    methods = []
    methods << :suspended if current_user&.trusted? || current_user&.any_admin?
    methods << :spam if current_user&.any_admin?

    options_to_merge = methods.empty? ? {} : { methods: methods }

    default_options.merge(options_to_merge)
  end

  before_action :authenticate_user!
  before_action :limit_uploads, only: [:create]

    authorize :image_upload

      invalid_image_error_message = validate_image

        respond_to do |format|

        end
        return
      end

      respond_to do |format|
        format.json do
          render json: { error: e.message }, status: :unprocessable_entity
        end
      end
      return
    rescue CarrierWave::ProcessingError # server error
      respond_to do |format|
        format.json do
          render json: { error: I18n.t("image_uploads_controller.server_error") },
                 status: :unprocessable_entity
        end
      end
      return
    end

    links = uploaders.map(&:url)
    respond_to do |format|
      format.json { render json: { links: links }, status: :ok }
    end
  end

  def limit_uploads
    rate_limit!(:image_upload)
  end

  def validate_image
    images = Array.wrap(params["image"])

    return is_not_file_message unless valid_image_files?(images)
    return filename_too_long_message unless valid_filenames?(images)

    nil

    images.none? { |image| !file?(image) }
  end

  def valid_filenames?(images)
    images.none? { |image| long_filename?(image) }
  end

  def upload_images(images)
    Array.wrap(images).map do |image|
      ArticleImageUploader.new.tap do |uploader|
        uploader.store!(image)
        rate_limiter.track_limit_by_action(:image_upload)
      end
    end
  end

**Deep Dive into Profile Picture Migration**

Okay, let's break this down systematically. We're tasked with migrating user and organization profile pictures from CarrierWave to Active Storage, one deployment at a time, without breaking existing pictures. The constraint is no downtime for existing images, and new uploads must use Active Storage.

First, this requires a phased approach.  We must:

1.  **Enable Active Storage.** This means installing the necessary Rails components, ensuring the database schema is up-to-date with Active Storage tables, and verifying the primary key types. I'll need to confirm versions, migrations, and database schema compatibility with the current Rails version. Checking `config/storage.yml` is critical, as well as environment configurations. We need to analyze dependencies like `aws-sdk-s3`, `image_processing`, and `marcel` to align with the existing infrastructure.

2.  **Ensure CarrierWave remains functional for other uploads.** This is about isolating the migration to *only* profile pictures. We must ensure the numerous other uploaders (images, cover photos, etc.) remain untouched, and their associated data continues to be managed by CarrierWave.  This is a significant factor in maintaining application stability.

3.  **Handle the existing `profile_image` column.**  This is the core challenge.  We *cannot* break existing profile picture URLs.  The key question is how to make Active Storage coexist with the existing CarrierWave data without introducing any data loss or breaks in the application. We need to understand how the database column (`users.profile_image`, `organizations.profile_image`) is used by both systems.  The two obvious options are to either have the new Active Storage attachment have a different name than the existing column, or to remove CarrierWave entirely from the model.

    The primary issue is the conflict arising from the `profile_image` and `profile_image=` methods.  CarrierWave already defines these on User and Organization models. Active Storage *also* defines the same, which leads to a collision.  Renaming the Active Storage attachment might seem like an option, but could cause a significant number of code changes, and potential bugs, by requiring code updates throughout the application.  It means searching the code for all instances of `user.profile_image = ...` and the like. We would need to identify *every* single place in the codebase where profile pictures are set and retrieved, including controllers, workers, factories, and external services.

    The alternative is to keep the Active Storage attachment named `profile_image`, and remove the CarrierWave `mount_uploader :profile_image` declaration.

    We need to check EVERY place in the code that uses the `profile_image` attribute. I need to understand exactly how the `profile_image` field is currently handled in the system (creation, updates, display, etc.) to guarantee backwards compatibility.

    We also need to understand how CarrierWave handles URLs and storage locations so that we can map them correctly to Active Storage, or transition existing URLs to use Active Storage in a later step.

Let's dive into the code and configurations to see how CarrierWave is configured.

class ArticleImageUploader < BaseUploader
  def store_dir
    "uploads/articles/"
  end

  def filename
    "#{Array.new(20) { rand(36).to_s(36) }.join}.#{file.extension}" if file.present?
  end

  def upload_from_url(url)
    # Open the URL and create a temporary file
    file = URI.open(url) # rubocop:disable Security/Open
    temp_file = Tempfile.new(["upload", File.extname(file.base_uri.path)])
    temp_file.binmode
    temp_file.write(file.read)
    temp_file.rewind

    # Upload the tempfile using CarrierWave
    store!(temp_file)

    # Important: Ensure you return the URL of the uploaded file
    stored_file_url = self.url # This should return the actual URL where the file is stored

    # Cleanup
    temp_file.close
    temp_file.unlink

    stored_file_url
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.error "Failed to handle file upload: #{e.message}"
    nil
  end
end

class BaseUploader < CarrierWave::Uploader::Base
  include CarrierWave::BombShelter  # limits size to 4096x4096
  include CarrierWave::MiniMagick   # adds processing operations

  EXTENSION_ALLOWLIST = %w[jpg jpeg jpe gif png ico bmp dng webp].freeze
  FRAME_MAX = 500
  FRAME_STRIP_MAX = 150

  process :validate_frame_count
  process :strip_exif

  def store_dir
    "uploads/#{model.class.to_s.underscore}/#{mounted_as}/#{model.id}"
  end

  def extension_allowlist
    EXTENSION_ALLOWLIST
  end

  def size_range
    1..(25.megabytes)
  end

  protected

  def strip_exif
    return if file.content_type.include?("svg")

    manipulate! do |image|
      image.auto_orient
      image.strip unless image.frames.count > FRAME_STRIP_MAX
      image = yield(image) if block_given?
      image
    end
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.error("Error stripping EXIF data: #{e}")
  end

  def validate_frame_count
    begin
      return unless MiniMagick::Image.new(file.path).frames.count > FRAME_MAX
    rescue Timeout::Error
      raise CarrierWave::IntegrityError, I18n.t("uploaders.base_uploader.timeout")
    end

    raise CarrierWave::IntegrityError,
          I18n.t("uploaders.base_uploader.too_many_frames", frame_max: FRAME_MAX)
  end
end

That `stub_request` in `spec/rails_helper.rb` for `dummyimage.com` is the culprit. Returning an empty body (`""`) in tests explains why CarrierWave was failing silently on `remote_profile_image_url=`, allowing the in-memory `user` object to have a seemingly set image URL without actually storing an image. This explains the discrepancies. And I see how this connects to the tests in `authenticator_spec.rb` where `expect(user.remote_profile_image_url).to eq(info.image)` fails.

Now, I need to understand how Active Storage fits into this mess, especially with `Images::Profile` and `Images::Optimizer`. Let's start with those services and then trace how Rails handles image URLs, specifically within the Active Storage context.

Looking at `Images::Optimizer.call`, I see a critical conditional: if the image source starts with `/`, it's returned as-is. This is key. The `config/initializers/carrierwave.rb` setups in development and test use relative URLs, like `/uploads/...`, while production uses absolute URLs from S3 (or a set `asset_host`).

Okay, now let's think about Active Storage: If I'm using `profile_image` attached with Active Storage, what URL is generated? `rails_blob_path` gives me a relative path (`/rails/...`), while `rails_blob_url` gives me an absolute path depending on the environment. I've got to check the `default_url_options`. In `test.rb`, it sets the host to `test.host`, but what happens in production? *Aha!* `production.rb` doesn't set a host for `default_url_options`! If I call `rails_blob_url` in a background job, mailer, serializer, or model in production, I'll get an `ArgumentError` because it's missing the host!

I need to look deeper. Let's inspect `app/lib/url.rb` to see how it handles domains and URLs, especially how it retrieves the application's domain. I suspect that this could be a point of divergence. Finally, let's examine other areas of the app like mailers, specs, and various views for where they're calling `profile_image_url` and `URL.local_image`.       when ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile
        blob.upload_without_unfurling(attachable.open)
      when Rack::Test::UploadedFile
        blob.upload_without_unfurling(
          attachable.respond_to?(:open) ? attachable.open : attachable

        blob.upload_without_unfurling(attachable)

In our tests, we're stubbing `skip_ssrf_protection?` to bypass the DNS lookup, and WebMock intercepts those calls.

The core question here is what happens when WebMock intercepts an image request (like `https://dummyimage.com/400x400.jpg`) and returns a 200 OK with an empty body. CarrierWave creates a `RemoteFile` with zero size. Does CarrierWave ignore empty files? Or does it attempt to store them? I need to check how the system reacts in the `authenticator_spec.rb` test and what's going on behind the scenes with the `CarrierWave::Downloader::Base`. I could print out the `user.profile_image_url` or look at `CarrierWave::Downloader::Base` to debug this.

My first thought is, let's carefully design the `remote_profile_image_url` setter!

I need to understand where that's actually used in the application.

What's interesting is that this service *either* returns a sanitized URL or a `File` object from `Images::ProfileImageGenerator.call` if the URL isn't HTTP. This is crucial! CarrierWave's setter might have been ignoring a non-string `File` here.

*   **Authentication Providers:** Providers like Facebook, GitHub, etc., all pass `remote_profile_image_url` through `new_user_data`, which is then used to initialize a new User.

*   **AI Profile Image Worker:** We're setting `user.remote_profile_image_url = result.url` here.

I need to nail down how this should behave, so let's think about how to define the `remote_profile_image_url` setter in `ProfileImageable`.

require 'open-uri'
require 'ssrf_filter'
require 'addressable'
require 'carrierwave/downloader/remote_file'

module CarrierWave
  module Downloader
    class Base
      include CarrierWave::Utilities::Uri

      attr_reader :uploader

      def initialize(uploader)
        @uploader = uploader
      end

      ##
      # Downloads a file from given URL and returns a RemoteFile.
      #
      # === Parameters
      #
      # [url (String)] The URL where the remote file is stored
      # [remote_headers (Hash)] Request headers
      #
      def download(url, remote_headers = {})
        @current_download_retry_count = 0
        headers = remote_headers.
          reverse_merge('User-Agent' => "CarrierWave/#{CarrierWave::VERSION}")
        uri = process_uri(url.to_s)
        begin
          if skip_ssrf_protection?(uri)
            response = OpenURI.open_uri(process_uri(url.to_s), headers)
          else
            request = nil
            if ::SsrfFilter::VERSION.to_f < 1.1
              response = SsrfFilter.get(uri, headers: headers) do |req|
                request = req
              end
            else
              response = SsrfFilter.get(uri, headers: headers, request_proc: ->(req) { request = req }) do |res|
                res.body # ensure to read body
              end
            end
            response.uri = request.uri
            response.value
          end
        rescue StandardError => e
          if @current_download_retry_count < @uploader.download_retry_count
            @current_download_retry_count += 1
            sleep @uploader.download_retry_wait_time
            retry
          else
            raise CarrierWave::DownloadError, "could not download file: #{e.message}"
          end
        end
        CarrierWave::Downloader::RemoteFile.new(response)
      end

      #
      # === Parameters
      #
      # [url (String)] The URL where the remote file is stored
      #
      def process_uri(source)
        uri = Addressable::URI.parse(source)
        uri.host = uri.normalized_host
        # Perform decode first, as the path is likely to be already encoded
        uri.path = encode_path(decode_uri(uri.path)) if uri.path =~ CarrierWave::Utilities::Uri::PATH_UNSAFE
        uri.query = encode_non_ascii(uri.query) if uri.query
        uri.fragment = encode_non_ascii(uri.fragment) if uri.fragment
        URI.parse(uri.to_s)
      rescue URI::InvalidURIError, Addressable::URI::InvalidURIError
        raise CarrierWave::DownloadError, "couldn't parse URL: #{source}"
      end

    extend ActiveSupport::Concern

      CarrierWave::Uploader::Base

      check_pixel_dimensions!(image)

    def check_image_type!(image)
      return if image.type && image_type_whitelist.include?(image.type)
      raise CarrierWave::IntegrityError,
            I18n.translate(:'errors.messages.unsupported_image_type')
    end

    def check_pixel_dimensions!(image)
      max_sizes = max_pixel_dimensions

      return if image.size &&
                image.size[0] <= max_sizes[0] &&
                image.size[1] <= max_sizes[1]

      raise CarrierWave::IntegrityError,
            I18n.translate(
              :'errors.messages.pixel_dimensions_error',
              x_size: max_sizes[0], y_size: max_sizes[1]

      return get_file(file.file) if is_wrapped?(file)

No query count specs, but I know optimizing these image fetches is crucial, especially in places where we iterate through lists of users or organizations.  Adding `.with_attached_profile_image` seems like the go-to solution to prevent N+1 queries. But I need to verify how this plays with `.select(...)`, which is common for performance reasons, because there are other optimizations here.

Let's dissect this. With Active Storage, the scope `with_attached_profile_image` uses `includes(profile_image_attachment: :blob)`.  The cool thing is, if I do a `select` like `Organization.select(:id, :name, :profile_image, ...).with_attached_profile_image`, the `includes` method runs separate `SELECT ... WHERE record_id IN (...)` queries, not a potentially problematic `JOIN`. So this is perfect.

Now for the critical edge case.  What if a user or organization still has an image path in the `profile_image` field from our legacy CarrierWave setup?  We have to ensure that old image URLs are handled correctly.  Let's look at the `ProfileImageUploader#url` method. If it finds a legacy filename:

  def legacy_profile_image_url
    legacy_filename = read_attribute(:profile_image)
    return if legacy_filename.blank?
    return legacy_filename if legacy_filename.start_with?("http://", "https://", "/")

    uploader = ProfileImageUploader.new(self, :profile_image)
    uploader.retrieve_from_store!(legacy_filename)
    uploader.url
  end

That critical line: `return legacy_filename if legacy_filename.start_with?("http://", "https://", "/")`.  Does that ever *actually* happen in a legitimate way with CarrierWave? No! CarrierWave file names are usually UUID based, like `53ee234e-e546-496f-8d33-8ec7f11ab0d2.jpeg`.  The only exceptions would be if the `profile_image` was set by something like `Moderator::BanishUser`, which uses a hardcoded URL.

If it *is* an external URL like `"https://..."`, then the code correctly returns that URL. This is correct behavior! Also, if it is a standard Carrierwave UUID style filename, the uploaders logic will correctly resolve the URL for development, production, and S3 usage.

Then the next question, which keeps me up at night: what if someone loads a model with `.select()` but *without* the `profile_image` field? Like, `User.select(:id, :username).find(1)`. When `profile_image_url` is called, will it crash?

We can avoid the crash using `has_attribute?(:profile_image)` and `read_attribute`. If that is false, then we return `nil`. If it's true, we need `read_attribute` to fetch the value and generate the correct URL. Note this avoid the `MissingAttributeError` caused by a missing attribute when using `Carrierwave`. We previously may have crashed there, but we won't now.

Now, let's consider the new scenario with Active Storage: What happens when the `profile_image` is attached and we're calling `Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.rails_blob_path`?  This is how it should work: If the blob is persisted: we need the right URL

The result from `rails_blob_path` is a relative path. In the production environment, the `URL.domain` check applies the correct base URL. What happens when we use a CDN or other image optimizers like `Images::Optimizer`? It will redirect through the redirect path and works with any set up.

And what about development and testing?  Returning the relative path from `rails_blob_path` works exactly like the old CarrierWave relative path which is exactly what we want.

      # for additional context)
      user_ids = result[:items].pluck(:user_id)

      # Only filter by subforem if we're not in the root subforem context

      relation = relation.cached_tagged_with(tags) if tags.any?

      # here we issue a COUNT(*) after all the conditions are applied,
      # because we need to fetch the total number of articles, pre pagination
      total = relation.count

      relation = relation.select(*ATTRIBUTES)
      relation = relation.page(page).per(per_page)

      {

# Handles profile image uploads via Active Storage while maintaining backwards-compatibility
# for existing CarrierWave `profile_image` records during the multi-deploy migration.
module ProfileImageable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  ALLOWED_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[
    image/jpeg
    image/jpg
    image/gif
    image/png
    image/x-icon
    image/vnd.microsoft.icon
    image/bmp
    image/x-ms-bmp
    image/x-adobe-dng
    image/webp
  ].freeze

  MAX_PIXEL_DIMENSIONS = [4096, 4096].freeze

  class << self
    def process_uploads?
      if @process_uploads.nil?
        !Rails.env.test?
      else
        @process_uploads
      end
    end

    attr_writer :process_uploads
  end

  included do
    has_one_attached :profile_image

    attr_reader :remote_profile_image_url

    before_save :track_and_clear_legacy_profile_image
    validate :validate_profile_image_attachment
  end

  def profile_image=(attachable)
    @profile_image_frame_error = nil
    @profile_image_download_error = nil

    if attachable.nil? || attachable == ""
      super
    elsif attachable.is_a?(String)
      blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.find_signed(attachable, record: self)
      super(blob) if blob
    else
      processed = ProfileImageable.process_uploads? ? process_profile_image_attachable(attachable) : attachable
      super(processed)
    end
  end

  def remote_profile_image_url=(url)
    @remote_profile_image_url = url
    @profile_image_download_error = nil

    return if url.blank?

    if url.respond_to?(:read) || url.is_a?(Pathname)
      self.profile_image = url
      return
    end

    return unless url.is_a?(String)

    uploader = ProfileImageUploader.new(self, :profile_image)
    remote_file = uploader.downloader.new(uploader).download(url)
    return if remote_file.size.zero?

    self.profile_image = {
      io: remote_file.file,
      filename: remote_file.original_filename.presence || "profile_image",
      content_type: remote_file.content_type
    }
  rescue CarrierWave::DownloadError => e
    @profile_image_download_error = e.message
  end

  def profile_image_url
    if profile_image_attached?
      active_storage_profile_image_url
    else
      legacy_profile_image_url
    end
  end

  def legacy_profile_image?
    return false if attachment_changes["profile_image"].is_a?(ActiveStorage::Attached::Changes::DeleteOne)

    has_attribute?(:profile_image) && read_attribute(:profile_image).present?
  end

  def serializable_hash(options = nil)
    hash = super
    hash["profile_image"] = { "url" => profile_image_url } if hash.key?("profile_image")
    hash
  end

  private

  def profile_image_attached?
    profile_image.respond_to?(:attached?) && profile_image.attached?
  end

  def profile_image_changed_for_save?
    saved_change_to_attribute?(:profile_image) || @profile_image_changed_in_save == true
  end

  def track_and_clear_legacy_profile_image
    change = attachment_changes["profile_image"]
    @profile_image_changed_in_save = change.present?

    if @profile_image_changed_in_save && has_attribute?(:profile_image)
      self[:profile_image] = nil
    end
  end

  def active_storage_profile_image_url
    return unless profile_image.blob&.persisted?

    path = Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.rails_blob_path(profile_image, only_path: true)
    if Rails.env.production? && URL.domain.present?
      URL.url(path)
    else
      path
    end
  end

  def legacy_profile_image_url
    return unless legacy_profile_image?

    legacy_filename = read_attribute(:profile_image)
    return legacy_filename if legacy_filename.start_with?("http://", "https://", "/")

    uploader = ProfileImageUploader.new(self, :profile_image)
    uploader.retrieve_from_store!(legacy_filename)
    uploader.url
  end

  def validate_profile_image_attachment
    if @profile_image_download_error.present?
      errors.add(:profile_image, @profile_image_download_error)
      return
    end

    change = attachment_changes["profile_image"]
    return unless change.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Attached::Changes::CreateOne)

    blob = change.blob
    max_size = ProfileImageUploader::MAX_FILE_SIZE

    if blob.byte_size < 1
      errors.add(:profile_image, "File size should be greater than 0 Bytes")
      return
    end

    if blob.byte_size > max_size
      errors.add(
        :profile_image,
        "File size should be less than #{ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_human_size(max_size)}",
      )
      return
    end

    extension = File.extname(blob.filename.to_s).delete_prefix(".").downcase
    if extension.present? && ProfileImageUploader::EXTENSION_ALLOWLIST.exclude?(extension)
      errors.add(
        :profile_image,
        I18n.t(
          "errors.messages.extension_allowlist_error",
          extension: extension.inspect,
          allowed_types: ProfileImageUploader::EXTENSION_ALLOWLIST.join(", "),
          default: "You are not allowed to upload %{extension} files, allowed types: %{allowed_types}",
        ),
      )
      return
    end

    if ALLOWED_CONTENT_TYPES.exclude?(blob.content_type)
      errors.add(
        :profile_image,
        I18n.t(
          "errors.messages.content_type_allowlist_error",
          content_type: blob.content_type,
          default: "is not an allowed image content type",
        ),
      )
      return
    end

    if @profile_image_frame_error.present?
      errors.add(:profile_image, @profile_image_frame_error)
      return
    end

    dimensions = extract_image_dimensions(change.attachable)
    if dimensions && (dimensions[0] > MAX_PIXEL_DIMENSIONS[0] || dimensions[1] > MAX_PIXEL_DIMENSIONS[1])
      errors.add(
        :profile_image,
        I18n.t(
          "errors.messages.pixel_dimensions_error",
          x_size: MAX_PIXEL_DIMENSIONS[0],
          y_size: MAX_PIXEL_DIMENSIONS[1],
          default: "dimensions are too large (max #{MAX_PIXEL_DIMENSIONS[0]}x#{MAX_PIXEL_DIMENSIONS[1]})",
        ),
      )
    end
  end

  def extract_image_dimensions(attachable)
    case attachable
    when Pathname
      File.open(attachable, "rb") { |f| FastImage.size(f) }
    when ActiveStorage::Blob
      attachable.open { |f| FastImage.size(f) } if attachable.persisted?
    else
      io = attachable_io(attachable)
      return unless io

      io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
      size = FastImage.size(io)
      io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
      size
    end
  end

  def attachable_io(attachable)
    case attachable
    when ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile, Rack::Test::UploadedFile
      attachable.respond_to?(:tempfile) ? attachable.tempfile : attachable.to_io
    when Hash
      attachable[:io]
    when File
      attachable
    end
  end

  def process_profile_image_attachable(attachable)
    return attachable if attachable.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Blob)

    io, filename, content_type, opened_io = extract_attachable_details(attachable)
    return attachable unless io && filename

    size = io_byte_size(io)
    return attachable unless size&.between?(1, ProfileImageUploader::MAX_FILE_SIZE)

    extension = File.extname(filename.to_s).delete_prefix(".").downcase
    return attachable if extension.present? && ProfileImageUploader::EXTENSION_ALLOWLIST.exclude?(extension)

    detected_type = content_type.presence || detect_content_type(io, filename)
    return attachable if ALLOWED_CONTENT_TYPES.exclude?(detected_type) || detected_type.include?("svg")

    tempfile = Tempfile.new(["profile_image", File.extname(filename.to_s)])
    tempfile.binmode
    io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
    IO.copy_stream(io, tempfile)
    io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
    tempfile.flush

    strip_exif_and_validate_frames(tempfile.path)

    tempfile.rewind
    { io: tempfile, filename: filename, content_type: detected_type }
  ensure
    opened_io&.close
  end

  def strip_exif_and_validate_frames(path)
    image = MiniMagick::Image.new(path)
    frames_count = image.frames.count
    if frames_count > BaseUploader::FRAME_MAX
      @profile_image_frame_error = I18n.t("uploaders.base_uploader.too_many_frames", frame_max: BaseUploader::FRAME_MAX)
    elsif frames_count <= BaseUploader::FRAME_STRIP_MAX
      image.auto_orient
      image.strip
    end
  rescue Timeout::Error
    @profile_image_frame_error = I18n.t("uploaders.base_uploader.timeout")
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.error("Error stripping EXIF data: #{e}")
  end

  def extract_attachable_details(attachable)
    case attachable
    when ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile, Rack::Test::UploadedFile
      io = attachable.respond_to?(:tempfile) ? attachable.tempfile : attachable.to_io
      [io, attachable.original_filename, attachable.content_type, nil]
    when Hash
      [attachable[:io], attachable[:filename], attachable[:content_type], nil]
    when File
      [attachable, File.basename(attachable.path), nil, nil]
    when Pathname
      opened = attachable.open("rb")
      [opened, attachable.basename.to_s, nil, opened]
    end
  end

  def io_byte_size(io)
    return io.size if io.respond_to?(:size)

    File.size(io.path) if io.respond_to?(:path) && io.path
  end

  def detect_content_type(io, filename)
    io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
    Marcel::MimeType.for(io, name: filename)
  ensure
    io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
  end
end

steps.reasoning_content:
**Test Results & Architectural Implications**

Wow, 491 out of 493 tests passed on the first run! That's impressive, but let's dive into those two failures, because they're pointing to some really interesting issues.

**Failure 1: EXIF Removal in `ProfileImageUploader`**

The first failure, in `spec/uploaders/profile_image_uploader_spec.rb:78`, regarding EXIF data removal, is exposing a subtle but important inconsistency.  We're seeing that the `ProfileImageUploader` tests, specifically for EXIF removal, aren't testing the uploader directly in this case.  It seems the tests are relying on a model (`User`) mounting the uploader and indirectly testing its behavior through that model's lifecycle (`user.profile_image = image_with_gps; user.save!`).  Since `ProfileImageUploader` is still used by several other models (`Tag`, `Tweet`, etc.), it's likely we haven't exercised EXIF removal properly. I'm thinking we need to make the tests for `ProfileImageUploader` explicitly target the uploader. Either we use `uploader.store!(image_with_gps)` (with `uploader.path`) OR utilize a model that *still* mounts the uploader (like `Tag` via `tag.profile_image = image_with_gps; tag.save!`). It's also making me think we *also* need dedicated specs for `ProfileImageable` EXIF removal, for `User` and `Organization`, setting `ProfileImageable.process_uploads = true`, and using `EXIFR::JPEG.new(StringIO.new(user.profile_image.download))` to ensure correct behavior.

**Failure 2: URL Generation with `build_stubbed` and Active Storage**

The second failure, in `spec/services/images/profile_spec.rb:33`, is revealing a critical misunderstanding about how Active Storage behaves with `build_stubbed`. The problem is that `build_stubbed(:user)` doesn't persist to the database.  This means that `user.profile_image_url` is returning `nil` when a model with Active Storage is built with a stub. Before, with CarrierWave, `build_stubbed(:user)` assigned `Rack::Test::UploadedFile` which triggered `cache!` synchronously and `uploader.url` returned a cached URL string. Now, with Active Storage, even if the image is attached (`profile_image.attached? == true`), the blob isn't persisted (`blob.persisted? == false`), and so the URL generating method returns `nil`. The service assumed the `profile_image_url` would be a non-nil string.

So, this highlights that our tests that use `build_stubbed(:user)` and expect a URL need careful examination. If we use `build_stubbed(:user)`, the profile image won't have a URL unless explicitly created in the test, so we either need to create (`create(:user)`) or stub with nil (`build_stubbed(:user, profile_image: nil)`). We can't generate a URL from an unpersisted `ActiveStorage::Blob` as it would be required to generate a `signed_id`. But even more worrying, are other specs using `build_stubbed` or `build` in the same way? Let's do a deep dive and grep through *all* our specs for `build_stubbed(:user`, `build(:user`, `build_stubbed(:organization`, and `build(:organization` with `profile_image`! And then run all the other specs we haven't checked to ensure consistent and correct behavior.

steps.reasoning_content:
**Test Results Analysis and Strategic Fixes**

Alright, let's break down these results. Looks like a clean sweep across a bunch of specs: `user_spec`, `organization_spec`, `user_profile_spec`, and the API specs. Excellent. We also have passing API v0 and v1 tests for users and followers, and docs for organizations and profile images. However, I need to note the `article_spec.rb` failures, which are unrelated and due to network issues within the container. I can probably stub those out to avoid future problems.

Now, the important part: We have a manageable set of failures from the change set. Specifically, three key areas we already knew about. 

1.  `registrations_spec.rb:130`:  This is Active Storage related (`User.last.profile_image.file.file`).
2.  `search_serializer_spec.rb:6`: Related to the profile image serialization using `profile_image_url`.
3.  `framework_defaults_spec.rb:147`: A configuration change is tripping this up.

On top of the failures, these are the other failures we previously identified:

4.  `profile_image_uploader_spec.rb:78`:  I need to rethink how the `ProfileImageUploader` is tested. Maybe test it directly or apply to a `Tag`? Also, I really need a dedicated `ProfileImageable` spec for EXIF removal on `User` and `Organization`.
5.  `images/profile_spec.rb:33`: Ah, this is critical, let's examine this carefully.

Let's dive into #5, which is particularly interesting. The test `spec/services/images/profile_spec.rb:33` is failing. Why? I see it now: `build_stubbed(:user)` in this context means the Active Storage blob isn't persisted. So, `user.profile_image_url` returns `nil`! This is because `profile_image.blob.persisted?` is `false`. The fix is obvious: change this to `create(:user)`. This will trigger the redirection URL, so `Images::Profile.call` will return the correct URL.

Thinking more broadly about this issue, is there ANY case in production where an unsaved `User` or `Organization` *should* have a profile image URL? No. In production, the URL is only assigned *after* the record is saved. Returning `nil` for unpersisted blobs is actually the correct behavior and helps avoid `ArgumentError` when using `build(:user)`. This logic will protect against unexpected issues in other tests like `spec/models/articles/cached_entity_spec.rb`.

So, the plan: Update the test to use `create(:user)` in `spec/services/images/profile_spec.rb` or check `user.profile_image_url` is present.

Now, before I sign off on this, I need to cover my bases. I'll execute the system specs for organization settings, search, mobile auth, bot creation, homepage, Liquid tags, and articles to verify that the fix and logic are sound.

Okay, 204 examples tested, and everything's green – no failures! That's a good start. Now, let's incorporate `.with_attached_profile_image` into all the relevant collection queries to optimize image loading. I need to make sure this is implemented where appropriate and that I test everything to prevent any regressions.

I'll start by adding the preload to the collection queries, then review the request specs. Specifically, I need to check `spec/requests/articles/*_spec.rb`, `spec/requests/admin/*`, `spec/requests/users*`, and `spec/uploaders/*` to ensure this change doesn't break anything. Next, I'll go through the remaining queries I identified earlier and add the preloads. I'll need to update the following files:

*   `app/controllers/api/v1/organizations_controller.rb`

**Refactoring Specs for Active Storage Migration**

Okay, time to get these specs updated for the Active Storage migration. I need to address those five specs that currently have CarrierWave-specific assertions. First:

1.  In `spec/uploaders/profile_image_uploader_spec.rb`, line 78, I should be testing the `ProfileImageUploader` by directly working with `uploader.store!(image_with_gps)` (or a `Tag` instance) instead of the `user` object. The `ProfileImageUploader` is still mounted on a number of models, and this change will better reflect that.
2.  In `spec/services/images/profile_spec.rb` on line 34, I need to make sure I create a persisted `user` with `create(:user)` and not `build_stubbed(:user)` since `build_stubbed` doesn't persist Active Storage blobs.
3.  For `spec/requests/registrations_spec.rb` on line 143, I need to verify that the `User`'s profile image is actually attached (`expect(User.last.profile_image).to be_attached`) and that the downloaded content matches the original file (`expect(User.last.profile_image.download).to eq(File.read(image_path, mode: "rb"))`).

require "rails_helper"
require "exifr/jpeg"

RSpec.describe ProfileImageable do
  let(:image_jpg) { fixture_file_upload("800x600.jpg", "image/jpeg") }
  let(:image_png) { fixture_file_upload("800x600.png", "image/png") }
  let(:image_webp) { fixture_file_upload("800x600.webp", "image/webp") }
  let(:image_pdf) { fixture_file_upload("800x600.pdf", "application/pdf") }
  let(:bad_image) { Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(Rails.root.join("spec/support/fixtures/images/bad-image.jpg"), "image/jpeg") }
  let(:image_with_gps) { fixture_file_upload("image_gps_data.jpg", "image/jpeg") }
  let(:high_frame_count) { fixture_file_upload("high_frame_count.gif", "image/gif") }

  describe "new uploads use Active Storage" do
    it "stores new user profile images in Active Storage and leaves legacy column nil", :aggregate_failures do
      user = create(:user, profile_image: image_jpg)

      expect(user.profile_image).to be_attached
      expect(user.read_attribute(:profile_image)).to be_nil
      expect(user.profile_image_url).to start_with("/rails/active_storage/blobs/")
      expect(user.profile_image_90).to eq(user.profile_image_url)
    end

    it "stores new organization profile images in Active Storage and leaves legacy column nil", :aggregate_failures do
      organization = create(:organization, profile_image: image_png)

      expect(organization.profile_image).to be_attached
      expect(organization.read_attribute(:profile_image)).to be_nil
      expect(organization.profile_image_url).to start_with("/rails/active_storage/blobs/")
      expect(organization.profile_image_90).to eq(organization.profile_image_url)
    end

    it "keeps other uploaders on CarrierWave", :aggregate_failures do
      tag = build(:tag)
      expect(tag.profile_image).to be_a(ProfileImageUploader)

      organization = build(:organization)
      expect(organization.cover_image).to be_a(CoverImageUploader)
    end
  end

  describe "existing CarrierWave profile images remain intact" do
    let(:legacy_filename) { "53ee234e-e546-496f-8d33-8ec7f11ab0d2.jpg" }

    it "serves the CarrierWave URL for a legacy user without an Active Storage attachment", :aggregate_failures do
      user = create(:user, profile_image: nil)
      user.update_columns(profile_image: legacy_filename)
      user.reload

      expect(user.profile_image).not_to be_attached
      expect(user.legacy_profile_image?).to be(true)
      expect(user.profile_image_url).to eq("/uploads/user/profile_image/#{user.id}/#{legacy_filename}")
      expect(user.profile_image_90).to eq("/uploads/user/profile_image/#{user.id}/#{legacy_filename}")
      expect(user.as_json["profile_image"]).to eq({ "url" => user.profile_image_url })
    end

    it "serves the CarrierWave URL and allows updates for a legacy organization", :aggregate_failures do
      organization = create(:organization)
      organization.profile_image.purge
      organization.update_columns(profile_image: legacy_filename)
      organization.reload

      expect(organization.profile_image).not_to be_attached
      expect(organization.legacy_profile_image?).to be(true)
      expect(organization.profile_image_url).to eq("/uploads/organization/profile_image/#{organization.id}/#{legacy_filename}")
      expect(organization.update(name: "Updated Legacy Org")).to be(true)
      expect(organization.reload.profile_image_url).to eq("/uploads/organization/profile_image/#{organization.id}/#{legacy_filename}")
    end

    it "moves a legacy user to Active Storage when a new profile image is uploaded", :aggregate_failures do
      user = create(:user, profile_image: nil)
      user.update_columns(profile_image: legacy_filename)
      user.reload

      allow(Users::BustProfileImageCacheWorker).to receive(:perform_async)
      user.update!(profile_image: image_webp)

      expect(user.reload.profile_image).to be_attached
      expect(user.read_attribute(:profile_image)).to be_nil
      expect(user.profile_image_url).to start_with("/rails/active_storage/blobs/")
      expect(Users::BustProfileImageCacheWorker).to have_received(:perform_async).with(user.id)
    end

    it "moves a legacy organization to Active Storage when a new profile image is uploaded", :aggregate_failures do
      organization = create(:organization)
      organization.profile_image.purge
      organization.update_columns(profile_image: legacy_filename)
      organization.reload

      organization.update!(profile_image: image_jpg)

      expect(organization.reload.profile_image).to be_attached
      expect(organization.read_attribute(:profile_image)).to be_nil
      expect(organization.profile_image_url).to start_with("/rails/active_storage/blobs/")
    end

    it "requires profile_image when explicitly cleared on a legacy organization" do
      organization = create(:organization)
      organization.profile_image.purge
      organization.update_columns(profile_image: legacy_filename)
      organization.reload

      organization.profile_image = nil
      expect(organization).not_to be_valid
      expect(organization.errors[:profile_image]).to be_present
    end
  end

  describe "validations and processing" do
    it "rejects unsupported file formats such as PDF" do
      user = build(:user, profile_image: image_pdf)
      expect(user).not_to be_valid
      expect(user.errors[:profile_image]).to be_present
    end

    it "rejects image bombs exceeding 4096x4096 pixels" do
      user = build(:user, profile_image: bad_image)
      expect(user).not_to be_valid
      expect(user.errors[:profile_image]).to be_present
    end

    it "ignores arbitrary non-signed strings without raising" do
      user = build(:user, profile_image: "https://example.com/some-image.png")
      expect(user.save).to be(true)
      expect(user.profile_image).not_to be_attached
    end

    context "when upload processing is enabled" do
      around do |example|
        previous = described_class.process_uploads?
        described_class.process_uploads = true
        example.run
      ensure
        described_class.process_uploads = previous
      end

      it "strips EXIF and GPS data on upload", :aggregate_failures do
        expect(EXIFR::JPEG.new(image_with_gps.path).exif?).to be(true)
        expect(EXIFR::JPEG.new(image_with_gps.path).gps.present?).to be(true)

        user = create(:user, profile_image: image_with_gps)
        downloaded = StringIO.new(user.profile_image.download)

        expect(EXIFR::JPEG.new(downloaded).exif?).to be(false)
        expect(EXIFR::JPEG.new(downloaded).gps.present?).to be(false)
      end

      it "rejects GIFs exceeding maximum frame count" do
        user = build(:user, profile_image: high_frame_count)
        expect(user).not_to be_valid
        expect(user.errors[:profile_image]).to include(/too many frames/i)
      end
    end
  end

  describe "remote_profile_image_url=" do
    it "downloads and attaches a valid remote image to Active Storage", :aggregate_failures do
      url = "https://example.com/avatar.png"
      stub_request(:get, url).to_return(
        status: 200,
        body: Rails.root.join("spec/fixtures/files/800x600.png").binread,
        headers: { "Content-Type" => "image/png" },
      )

      user = create(:user, profile_image: nil, remote_profile_image_url: url)

      expect(user.profile_image).to be_attached
      expect(user.profile_image_url).to start_with("/rails/active_storage/blobs/")
    end

    it "adds a validation error when remote download fails" do
      url = "https://example.com/missing.png"
      stub_request(:get, url).to_return(status: 404, body: "Not Found")

      user = build(:user, profile_image: nil, remote_profile_image_url: url)

      expect(user).not_to be_valid
      expect(user.errors[:profile_image]).to be_present
    end
  end

  describe "Moderator::BanishUser" do
    it "purges the Active Storage attachment and falls back to DEFAULT_PROFILE_IMAGE", :aggregate_failures do
      admin = create(:user, :super_admin)
      user = create(:user, profile_image: image_jpg)
      expect(user.profile_image).to be_attached

      Moderator::BanishUser.call(admin: admin, user: user)
      user.reload

      expect(user.profile_image).not_to be_attached
      expect(user.profile_image_url).to eq(Moderator::BanishUser::DEFAULT_PROFILE_IMAGE)
    end
  end
end
EOF

steps.message: Let's fix the stale-inode issue in `app/models/concerns/profile_imageable.rb` by reading the processed file into `StringIO` and closing/unlinking the tempfile cleanly, and update `profile_imageable_spec.rb`.
steps.reasoning_content:
**The Eureka Moment: Fixing the EXIF Data Persistence Bug**

Right, let's see. I've been digging into this image processing issue, and I think I've just cracked it! It all started with the `article_image_uploader_spec.rb` and the `stub_const("BaseUploader::FRAME_MAX", 20)` line. Then, the comparison between `User.create!` and the successful `res` where EXIF data was stripped, but the former was not. I was trying to understand *why* the EXIF data was persisting in one case and not the other.

Aha! `create_one.rb` and that `tempfile` variable. In `process_profile_image_attachable(attachable)`, we're passing the `tempfile` to the `ActiveStorage::Blob` creation. I confirmed that `ProfileImageable#profile_image=` *was* being called during the `User.create!` operation, so the image processing flow was being correctly invoked. Then I saw the byte sizes and that's when things started to click, and I knew I was on to something!

The `dl` object had 161713 bytes (exif? true), while `res[:io]` had exif after process? false.

I went to `rails runner` and checked what `u.profile_image=` was doing with the processed image. Then the code path! `u.profile_image = processed` -> `CreateOne.new("profile_image", self, processed)` -> `ActiveStorage::Blob.build_after_unfurling(io: tempfile, ...)`!

My attention was drawn to this line: `MiniMagick::Image.new(tempfile.path)`. Now, the key is the `tempfile.size` *after* `MiniMagick`'s `mogrify` command runs on that `tempfile.path`. Bingo!

`tempfile` is an *open* Ruby `Tempfile`, pointing to the file at `tempfile.path`. But `MiniMagick`'s `mogrify` command is running an *external* `mogrify` and *replaces* the file at `tempfile.path` with a *new* inode (unlink + rename). The open Ruby `Tempfile` file descriptor *still* points to the *old*, unlinked inode—which still has the EXIF data! Meanwhile, the new stripped file is at the same path!

That's the bug! **Insane catch!** `mogrify` writes to a temp file and renames it over `tempfile.path`, so the original file descriptor is pointing to the old unstripped inode.

The solution? Easy: reopen `File.open(tempfile.path, "rb")` (or `File.binread(tempfile.path)` and wrap it in a `StringIO`) *after* the `strip_exif_and_validate_frames(tempfile.path)` call. Then close and unlink the `tempfile` in an `ensure` block!

This approach gives us three key benefits:

1.  No leaked tempfiles on disk!
2.  No stale-inode bug!
3.  `StringIO` will work seamlessly with `FastImage.size`, `rewind`, `CreateOne`, `ActiveStorage::Blob.build_after_unfurling`, and the upload!

Let's verify this, and let's update `profile_imageable_spec.rb` to add `stub_const("BaseUploader::FRAME_MAX", 20)` and use fresh `StringIO.new(user.profile_image.download)` for both `EXIFR::JPEG.new` checks. Perfect! I think we've got this one solved.

steps.reasoning_content:
**Expanding Profile Image Handling with Robust Testing**

Okay, 343 examples and no failures so far – that's a good sign! Time to really push the boundaries of this `profile_imageable_spec.rb` and nail down some critical edge cases. I need to be absolutely sure this image handling is bulletproof.

First, I need tests covering the Active Storage URL in a production environment. I'll need to simulate that `Rails.env.production?` scenario, specifically testing how `URL.url(...)` behaves. Then, I have to ensure we're properly handling those legacy CarrierWave URLs, particularly when `CarrierWave` is configured for those "forem_cloud" or "standard_production_config" scenarios. I'll focus on testing `legacy_profile_image_url` and verifying the delegation of `ProfileImageUploader#url`.

Next up, I absolutely have to validate this end-to-end. I'm thinking request/controller tests are the way to go here. I'll need to cover these specific endpoints:

*   A `PUT /users/:id.json` test to confirm that the onboarding JS is getting the Active Storage URL back in the response. Specifically, `json["user"]["profile_image"]["url"]` should be correct.
*   A `GET /api/organizations` test, making sure it returns both legacy CarrierWave *and* new Active Storage organizations with valid `profile_image["url"]`.
*   A `PATCH /settings/organization/:slug` test to verify that updating a name on a legacy CarrierWave org *without* uploading a new image doesn't break anything and the legacy profile picture remains intact.
*   Tests for both `POST /api/organizations` and `PUT /api/organizations/:id`
*   A check for a `User` with legacy CarrierWave `profile_image` updating their `name` and ensuring the legacy `profile_image` is preserved.

I'll add these new specs directly to `spec/models/concerns/profile_imageable_spec.rb` (or potentially a dedicated request spec block within it). And of course, after making all these changes, I'll run RuboCop to make sure I haven't introduced any style violations. We have to keep things clean and maintainable.

arguments.command:
cat <<'EOF' >> spec/models/concerns/profile_imageable_spec.rb

RSpec.describe "ProfileImageable integration", type: :request do
  let(:image_jpg) { fixture_file_upload("800x600.jpg", "image/jpeg") }
  let(:legacy_filename) { "53ee234e-e546-496f-8d33-8ec7f11ab0d2.jpg" }

  describe "JSON and API responses for mixed CarrierWave and Active Storage records" do
    it "returns Active Storage URL in PUT /users/:id.json response for onboarding uploader", :aggregate_failures do
      user = create(:user)
      sign_in user

      put "/users/#{user.id}.json", params: { user: { profile_image: image_jpg } }

      expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
      json = response.parsed_body
      expect(json["success"]).to be(true)
      expect(json.dig("user", "profile_image", "url")).to start_with("/rails/active_storage/blobs/")
      expect(user.reload.profile_image).to be_attached
    end

    it "serves both legacy CarrierWave and new Active Storage orgs in GET /api/organizations", :aggregate_failures do
      active_org = create(:organization, profile_image: image_jpg)
      legacy_org = create(:organization)
      legacy_org.profile_image.purge
      legacy_org.update_columns(profile_image: legacy_filename)

      get "/api/organizations", headers: { "Accept" => "application/vnd.forem.api-v1+json" }

      expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
      by_id = response.parsed_body.index_by { |org| org["id"] }
      expect(by_id[active_org.id].dig("profile_image", "url")).to start_with("/rails/active_storage/blobs/")
      expect(by_id[legacy_org.id].dig("profile_image", "url")).to eq(
        "/uploads/organization/profile_image/#{legacy_org.id}/#{legacy_filename}",
      )
    end

    it "preserves legacy profile image when updating other settings on a legacy organization", :aggregate_failures do
      user = create(:user, :org_admin)
      organization = user.organizations.first
      organization.profile_image.purge
      organization.update_columns(profile_image: legacy_filename)
      sign_in user

      patch "/settings/organization/#{organization.id}", params: {
        organization: { name: "Renamed Org" }
      }

      expect(response).to redirect_to(organization_settings_path(organization.slug))
      organization.reload
      expect(organization.name).to eq("Renamed Org")
      expect(organization.profile_image).not_to be_attached
      expect(organization.profile_image_url).to eq(
        "/uploads/organization/profile_image/#{organization.id}/#{legacy_filename}",
      )
    end
  end

  describe "production URL formatting" do
    it "prepends full domain URL for Active Storage blobs in production" do
      user = create(:user, profile_image: image_jpg)
      allow(Rails.env).to receive(:production?).and_return(true)
      allow(URL).to receive(:domain).and_return("forem.example.com")
      allow(URL).to receive(:url).and_call_original

      expect(user.profile_image_url).to start_with("http://forem.example.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/").or(
        start_with("https://forem.example.com/rails/active_storage/blobs/"),
      )
    end
  end
end
EOF
